narrative.overview:
The page is set like the lab the best project came from. In the light theme it is agar under lab light: a sage page with soft white pools of light and moss-green ink. In the dark theme it is a scanner bed: near-black green with lighter green reflections and a fine grain, and sage ink. Both keep safranin, the red stain used on plant tissue, as the one accent, and it only marks things you can press or that show where you are.

Names and titles are set in a serif, Source Serif 4; everything you read is in Archivo. Each project opens with its serif title, then one short highlighted key result, then a sentence or two, with the rest behind Read more or on the project's own page. Key words are bold in full ink, so a skimmer can read only those and still get the story.

The page is built from a few repeated pieces: a floating pill navigation, sections that each open with a centred heading and one intro sentence, and cards that are a little lighter than what sits behind them. Tokens live in `src/index.css`; the shared link and button classes in `src/components/linkStyles.ts`. Components use token class names (`text-ink`, `bg-accent`, `text-project`, `rounded-card`) and never raw colours.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes from one set of colour names, switched by `data-theme` on `<html>`. The visitor's device setting decides by default; the switch overrides it and is remembered.
Safranin only on buttons, active states, icons and links. Charts and diagrams are drawn in ink.
Serif for the name, section headings, project titles and the closing email; Archivo for reading and small bold labels.
Sections alternate between the page tone and the slightly darker band tone.
Short text everywhere; detail lives behind Read more or on a project page, jargon behind a tap-or-hover explanation.

rules.name: The Accent Jobs Rule
rules.body: Red appears only on buttons, active states, icons and links. Diagram marks, chart bars, steps and client logos are ink (a logo takes the text colour beside it). Red has named jobs: `accent` fills, `accent-line` draws focus outlines and icons, `accent-text` colours text, `accent-tint` sits behind icons and the active link. On a dark ground `accent-text` is the ink colour, because a red light enough to read as text turns pink there.

rules.name: The Lighter Card Rule
rules.body: A card is always a little lighter than what is behind it: `surface` is lighter than both `page` and `band` in both themes, so a card reads as a card on either section tone.

rules.name: The Contrast Pairs Rule
rules.body: New colour values must pass these pairs, measured on the shipped values. Text: ink at least 9:1 on page, band and surface (light 10.3, 9.6, 11.3; dark 15.7, 14.6, 12.9); ink-soft at least 4.5:1 on all three (light 5.9, 5.5, 6.5; dark 10.4, 9.7, 8.6); white on accent and accent-hover at least 4.5:1 (light 6.6 and 8.8; dark 5.2 and 6.7). Lines and icons at least 3:1: accent-line (light 5.1 to 6.0; dark 4.1 to 5.0) and bar-muted (light 3.4 to 4.0; dark 4.1 to 5.0).

rules.name: The No Flat Page Rule
rules.body: The page is never one flat colour. `--reflection` paints faint light pools on a fixed layer behind everything (`body::before`): white at 0.5 to 0.65 opacity and one moss shadow at 0.07 in light; green at 0.16 to 0.22 plus a grain and a faint sheen in dark. New pools reuse these tints.

rules.name: The Key Result Rule
rules.body: Every project reads title, then key result, then description. The key result is one short line with a soft ink highlighter behind it (`.key-result-mark`, ink at 8%, wrapping line by line); its number is marked `**bold**` in `src/data/projects.ts` and rendered at weight 800, the heaviest text in the project. The title stays larger than the key result.

rules.name: The Key Word Rule
rules.body: Mark key words in the data files with `**double asterisks**`; `Rich.tsx` renders them bold in full ink while the sentence stays ink-soft. A few words per sentence, never a whole sentence.

rules.name: The Readable Text Rule
rules.body: Strong contrast, body text left-aligned, lines at most about 70 characters (`max-w-measure`, 33rem). Only section headings, intros and Contact are centred. Headings use `text-wrap: balance` and paragraphs `text-wrap: pretty`; `keepTogether()` in `src/lib/text.ts` glues numbers to units and keeps names whole. Headings never break one word per line on phones: the display and section sizes shrink with the window down to 320px.

rules.name: The Glossary Rule
rules.body: Technical terms are written `[[term]]` in the data files and explained in plain language from `src/data/glossary.ts`. `Term.tsx` shows the explanation in a small ink bubble on tap, hover or keyboard focus, and screen readers always hear it.

rules.name: The Floating Layer Rule
rules.body: Only things that float over the page (the nav pill, its menu, the glossary bubble), the controls laid over a picture (the Pause button, the play badge) and the photo cast a soft shadow. Cards never do, not even on hover; they get their edge from tone and the inset hairline.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: Every card, panel, photo, screenshot and tooltip uses `rounded-card` (1.25rem). Buttons, nav links, tags and skill chips are pills (`rounded-full`). Smaller fixed shapes: icon tiles 12px, the key-result highlight 6px, chart bar tips 4px. Circles carry meaning in diagrams: filled ink dots are the owner's steps, outlined dots the team's. Lines are 2px in ink at 50 to 60%.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: A project's main visual shows the work: a screenshot, a recording, a chart of approved numbers or a how-it-works diagram. A logo names the client but is not evidence, so it is never a project's main visual (the owner's rule, 2026-10-18). Client logos appear only small, in the text colour, beside the client's name (`ClientLogo.tsx`).

dos: Do use the semantic colour names so a block works in both themes without extra code, and check new values against The Contrast Pairs Rule on page, band and surface.
Do open every new section with `Section.tsx`: heading, one intro sentence in `src/data/site.ts`, and the next tone in the page/band alternation.
Do give every project its serif title, then its key result, then one or two sentences; put the rest behind Read more or on its project page.
Do lead a project with evidence of the work; show the client's logo only small, in the text colour, beside the client's name.
Do keep body text left-aligned in `max-w-measure`, and mark key words with `**` and jargon with `[[ ]]` in the data files.
Do put new motion in `src/index.css` inside the reduced-motion media query, and animate in the direction the data flows.
Do draw his own work as filled nodes and the team's as outlined nodes, with the legend and spoken labels; give every chart a hidden table.
Do add `forced-colors:` system colours to any new drawn line or dot.
donts: Don't use red in charts, diagrams or text that isn't a link; red is for buttons, active states, icons and links.
Don't give a card a darker fill than its ground, a different corner radius, or a drop shadow.
Don't use square or slightly rounded buttons or chips; they are pills.
Don't add a third font family, or set body text in the serif.
Don't let a key result or anything else in a project grow larger than its title.
Don't write more than one or two sentences on a card or row.
Don't set a colour with a raw hex in a component; add or reuse a token in `src/index.css`.
Don't plot numbers that are not approved, or put two different tests in one chart.
Don't make a logo a project's main visual, or show it in its own colours.
